Document: Practice Direction 51R – Online Civil Money Claims Pilot
Part 6 of 10
==================================================
[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.38A Where—] Court to ask the claimant for their response, and claimant’s response

## 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (a) the part admission in full settlement of the claim; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (b) any repayment plan,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] or whether they reject the part admission and wish to continue with the claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (2) The claimant accepts or rejects the part admission and repayment terms (if relevant) by completing form OCON225A, and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website where none of the parties is represented by a legal representative, or if the claimant is, or all the parties are, legally represented, by the claimant accepting or rejecting the part admission and repayment terms using the relevant screens on the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] The claimant accepts the part admission with payment within 5 days

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] 7.40(1) This paragraph applies if the claimant accepts the part admission in full settlement of the claim where the defendant has offered to pay the amount admitted so that it is received within 5 days of the date of the part admission. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (2) The part admission is treated as if there had been no part defence as well. The court must inform the parties of this. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (3) If the claimant uses form OCON225A or the relevant screens on the OCMC website (as appropriate) to accept the defendant’s offer of the amount admitted in full settlement of the claim, but then the claimant has not received the whole amount admitted before the end of the 5 days, the claimant may request a judgment on admission. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (4) The claimant requests the judgment by completing form OCON225A and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website where none of the parties is represented by a legal representative, or if the claimant is, or all the parties are, legally represented, by the claimant requesting judgment using the relevant screens on the OCMC website. When requesting judgment, the claimant may also specify its repayment plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (5) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (6) If the claimant has specified a repayment plan in the request for judgment, the judgment must state that repayment is to be made in accordance with that repayment plan, unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in the repayment plan has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (6A) If a repayment date specified in the repayment plan has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that repayment plan, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (a) if the repayment plan states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (b) if the repayment plan states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment, and with subsequent instalments to be paid at one calendar month intervals after that. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (7) If the claimant has not specified a repayment plan in the request for judgment, the judgment must state that the whole amount admitted must be repaid immediately. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (8) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (a) the amount admitted;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (b) any interest on the amount admitted that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (c) court fees, and any fixed costs that the claimant is entitled to in accordance with Section 2B,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] minus any payments of the amount admitted on the response form (as defined) that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees or fixed costs, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] The claimant accepts the part admission and repayment plan

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] 7.41(1) This paragraph applies if the claimant accepts the part admission and in full settlement of the claim where the defendant has asked for more than 5 days to pay. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (2) The part admission is treated as if there had been no part defence as well, and paragraphs 7.41A to 7.41D apply. The court must inform the parties of this. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] Claimant accepts part admission and repayment plan – claimant may request judgment on admission

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] 7.41A If the claimant uses OCON225A or the relevant screens on the OCMC website (as appropriate) to accept the defendant’s offer of the amount admitted in full settlement of the claim and proposed repayment plan, the claimant may request a judgment on admission, but does not have to: if none of the parties is represented by a legal representative, the claimant may decide to propose a settlement agreement instead. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] Claimant accepts part admission and repayment plan and decides to request a judgment on admission

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] 7.41B(1) If the claimant decides to request judgment on admission, the claimant requests the judgment by completing form OCON225A and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website where none of the parties is represented by a legal representative, or if the claimant is, or all the parties are, legally represented, by the claimant requesting judgment using the relevant screens on the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (2) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (3) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (a) the amount admitted;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (b) any interest on the amount admitted that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (c) court fees, and any fixed costs that the claimant is entitled to in accordance with Section 2B,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] minus any payments of the amount admitted on the response form (as defined) that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees or fixed costs, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (4) The judgment must state that the amount is to be paid in accordance with the defendant’s repayment plan, unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in the repayment plan has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (5) If a repayment date specified in the defendant’s repayment plan has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that repayment plan, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (a) if the repayment plan states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] (b) if the repayment plan states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment, and with subsequent instalments to be paid at one calendar month intervals after that. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.39(1) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept–] Claimant accepts part admission and repayment plan, proposes a settlement agreement instead of requesting a judgment on admission – defendant accepts the proposal for a settlement agreement

## 7.41C (1) If –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (a)  the claimant accepts the defendant’s offer and proposed repayment plan;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (za) none of the parties is represented by a legal representative;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (b) instead of requesting a judgment on admission, the claimant has proposed a settlement agreement on the same terms as the defendant’s proposed repayment plan;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (c) the proposed agreement is in the form of OCON Settlement Agreement A;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (d) the claimant has used the OCMC website to notify the court of the proposal to the defendant; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (e) the defendant has, within 7 days of the date of the claimant’s proposal, used the OCMC website to notify the court that they have accepted the proposal and agree to the settlement agreement, the court must “stay” the proceedings (as defined). When it stays the proceedings,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] the court must enable the claimant to return to court to request judgment on admission for any money still owed under the settlement agreement, if the settlement agreement breaks down, and the defendant fails to comply with the settlement agreement. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (2) If the settlement agreement breaks down, the claimant requests judgment on admission by completing form OCON225 and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (3) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (4) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (a) the amount admitted;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (b) any interest on the amount admitted that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (c) court fees,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] minus any payments of the amount admitted on the response form (as defined) that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (5) The judgment must state that the amount is to be paid in accordance with the terms of the settlement agreement, unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in the settlement agreement has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (6) If a repayment date specified in the settlement agreement has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that settlement agreement, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (a) if the settlement agreement states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] (b) if the settlement agreement states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment, and with subsequent instalments to be paid at one calendar month intervals after that. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41C (1) If –] Claimant accepts the defendant’s proposed repayment plan, proposes a settlement agreement, instead of requesting a judgment on admission – defendant rejects the proposal for a settlement agreement, or does not respond

## 7.41D (1) If –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (a)  the claimant accepts the defendant’s offer and proposed repayment plan;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (za) none of the parties is represented by a legal representative;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (b) instead of requesting a judgment on admission, the claimant has proposed a settlement agreement on the same terms as the defendant’s proposed repayment plan;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (c) the proposed agreement is in the form of OCON Settlement Agreement A;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (d) the claimant has used the OCMC website to notify the court of the proposal to the defendant; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (e) the defendant has, within 7 days of the date of the claimant’s proposal, used the OCMC website to notify the court that they have rejected the proposal and do not agree to the settlement agreement, or within that time has failed to notify the court of their response, the claimant may request a judgment on admission. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (2) The claimant requests a judgment on admission by completing form OCON225 and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (3) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (4) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (a) the amount admitted;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (b) any interest on the amount admitted that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (c) court fees,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] minus any payments of the amount admitted on the response form (as defined) that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (5) The judgment must state that the amount is to be paid in accordance with the defendant’s proposed repayment plan, unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in the repayment plan has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (6) If a repayment date specified in the defendant’s repayment plan has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that repayment plan, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (a) if the repayment plan states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.41D (1) If –] (b) if the repayment plan states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment, and with subsequent instalments to be paid at one calendar month intervals after that. ## 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (1) This paragraph applies if the claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan where the defendant has asked for more than 5 days to pay. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (2) The part admission is treated as if there had been no part defence as well, and paragraphs 7.42A to 7.42F apply if the defendant is an individual, which includes a sole trader, and paragraph 7.42G applies if the defendant is not an individual. The court must inform the parties of this. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] Defendant offers to pay amount admitted and proposed repayment plan – claimant accepts offer but not the repayment plan, proposes different plan; defendant is an individual, which includes a sole trader: affordability calculation

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] 7.42A-(1) If the claimant has rejected the defendant’s proposed repayment plan, the claimant may also suggest a repayment plan. If the claimant suggests a repayment plan then—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (a) if all the parties are represented by a legal representative or the claimant is represented by a legal representative and the defendant is not represented by a legal representative then the claim will be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims and sub-paragraphs (2)-(5) and paragraphs 7.42B-F will not apply;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (b) otherwise, sub-paragraphs (2)-(5) will apply. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (2) On receiving the claimant’s suggested repayment plan, the court will produce an “affordability calculation”. The affordability calculation will be carried out electronically, by the application of a formula to the information submitted by the parties. The purpose of the calculation is to establish what rate of repayment a defendant is likely to be able to afford, based on the information submitted by the parties: an “affordability calculation repayment plan”. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (3) The explanation of the formula is set out in Annex A to this practice direction. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (4) If the affordability calculation indicates that the defendant will not be able to afford to repay the amount admitted in accordance with the claimant’s repayment plan, the court will tell the claimant, and ask the claimant whether they accept or reject the affordability calculation repayment plan instead. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (5) The claimant may accept or reject the affordability calculation repayment plan using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] Claimant accepts affordability calculation repayment plan or the affordability calculation repayment plan amounts to the claimant’s proposed repayment plan – court asks claimant whether they request judgment, or are proposing a settlement agreement instead

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] 7.42B If the claimant accepts the affordability calculation repayment plan, or if the affordability calculation repayment plan is calculated as amounting to the claimant’s repayment plan, the court will ask the claimant whether they wish to request judgment on admission, or whether they are proposing a settlement agreement instead. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] Claimant accepts affordability calculation repayment plan or affordability calculation repayment plan amounts to the claimant’s proposed repayment plan – claimant requests judgment

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] 7.42C-(1) If, after an affordability calculation has been done and the court has asked the claimant how they wish to proceed, the claimant wishes to request a judgment on admission, they may make the request by completing form OCON225A and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (2) If the court receives a request for judgment, it must “enter judgment” (as defined)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (3) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (a) the amount admitted;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (b) any interest on the amount admitted that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (c) court fees,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] minus any payments of the amount admitted on the response form (as defined) that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (4) The judgment must state that the amount is to be paid in accordance with the affordability calculation repayment plan(as defined), unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in the affordability calculation repayment plan has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (4A) If a repayment date specified in the affordability calculation repayment plan has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that repayment plan, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (a) if the repayment plan states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (b) if the repayment plan states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment, and with subsequent instalments to be paid at one calendar month intervals after that. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (5) If, after judgment has been made, the defendant objects to the affordability calculation repayment plan, or if the claimant no longer agrees to the plan, they may ask, on time, for a redetermination by a judge of the plan for the repayment of the amount admitted by the defendant. The claimant or defendant may make their request for redetermination to the court, by email to the OCMC email address, or on paper to the OCMC postal address (as defined). When requesting a redetermination, the claimant or defendant must explain why they object to the affordability calculation repayment plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (6) The request for redetermination will be submitted to the court on time if it is received by the court within 19 days after the date of the judgment. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (7) If the court receives a request for redetermination on time, it must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims to the defendant’s “home court” (as defined).
